chunks: 5472 - In the book of Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah have mercy on him: from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from his two brothers Muḥammad and Aḥmad, from their father, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:

A man died and appointed two men as executors. One of them said to his companion, “Take half of what he left, and give me half of what he left.” But the other refused him. So they asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about that, and he said:

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one asked for the ruling
key_terms.أَوْصَى إِلَى رَجُلَيْنِ: appointed two men as executors of the will
key_terms.ذَاكَ لَهُ: that right belongs to him; the claim is affirmed
key_terms.نِصْفَ مَا تَرَكَ: half of the estate left by the deceased

ai.seo_question: If two men are appointed as executors of a will, may one take charge of half of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question concerning two jointly appointed executors of a deceased person’s estate. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules in favor of the executor’s claim to divide responsibility and possession by half, indicating the validity of such an arrangement in administering the bequest.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5472 - In the book of Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub Al-Kulayni (may Allah (swt) have mercy on him), narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithami, from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad, from their father, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Burayd ibn Muawiyah, it is reported:

A man passed away and appointed two individuals as executors of his will. One of them said to his companion, "Take half of what he left behind, and give me the other half."
However, the other refused.
They sought guidance from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding this matter, and Imam (as) said:
